Subject: Request: short-term routing agent for log ingestion

Hi Vivek,

Hope you’re well — we’re running a limited cutover for a few customers this week and need to add EdgeFlux as a temporary routing agent to accept obfuscated telemetry and delivery acknowledgements for three tenants in us-west-2. This would be a short-term subprocessor addition (expected 4–6 weeks) and we wanted to confirm Redwood’s process so we can be live by Monday.

Can you confirm:
- Required evidence for onboarding (SOC2/ISO? network diagram?)
- Whether a temporary DPA addendum or a signed SOW is needed for a 1-month placement
- Any IP range or egress constraints we should follow for the test window

We’re prepared to share an inventory + network diagram. Attaching the roster and a high-level network sketch.

Thanks,
Maya Suri
Head of Partnerships, EdgeFlux

Thanks Maya — received and appreciate the quick heads-up. A few initial notes to get this moving: 

1) Evidence: We need the SOC 2 Type II report or a signed System Security Attestation, plus the completed subprocessor checklist. The network diagram is helpful; please mark the paths that touch customer payloads.

2) Legal / Process: For a temporary 4–6 week placement we usually do a one-page DPA addendum plus the standard subprocessor notification. Legal will review the addendum; please prepare to accept Redwood’s security addendum with the temporary-scope clause.

3) Egress: For the test window we can whitelist the subnets you supply, but Rishi should confirm whether there are any cross-border flows.

Kimberly — looping you in to run through SOC/attestation requirements and to confirm the minimal evidence we need to greenlight the temporary add.
Rishi — can you confirm egress and the rollback constraints (network and KV cache clearance)?

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya / team,

Quick checklist for a temporary subprocessor add (what will unblock us):
- SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) OR completed Security Attestation form
- Completed Subprocessor Security Checklist (I’ve attached our template below)
- Network diagram with egress/country labels and the three tenant IDs called out
- Proposed DPA addendum signed (we can provisionally approve pending Legal stamp)

If you can provide the two evidentiary docs (SOC2 or attestation + completed roster checklist) we can run a 48–72h tech review. Note: for temporary agents we limit access to obfuscated telemetry only and we will configure strict TTLs on caches.

Also tagging Laura to confirm if any customer-specific approvals are required for these tenants.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term routing agent for log ingestion

Maya / team — technical ops notes and rollback plan: 

- Egress/Residency: From the attachments it looks like EdgeFlux keeps processing inside us-west-2. That’s acceptable for the customers named, but we need a signed attestation that no telemetry will be routed through any eu/apac endpoints.
- Cache/Keys: We will apply KV cache eviction at cutback. Please confirm you’ll honour a zero-retention mode on Redwood-provisioned keys for the relevant tenant IDs.
- Rollback choreography (high level):
  1) Disable routing policy in Canary pool (0–5 minutes)
  2) Flush KV caches tied to tenant IDs (5–15 minutes)
  3) Revoke EdgeFlux subprocessor ACLs and confirm via signed webhook (15–30 minutes)
  4) Run integrity sweep for duplicate ACKs/ingestion discrepancies (30–60 minutes)

We’ll only greenlight the change after: SOC2 or attestation, completed checklist, and an executed DPA addendum that explicitly captures the rollback obligations above.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
